digest.component_or_area: comment hygiene detector and CI guard
propositions: Source comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run IDs, and dated incident narratives that decay due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit and retention window expiry.

A net-new block-level detector scans for rot-prone tokens: SHA-like hex (≥7 chars, digits+letters), run/job/thread IDs (≥8 digits), and date+incident-verb pairs; it accepts blocks citing ticket IDs (4x4 hex or word-triple aliases) or carrying 'context: external' escape hatch.

All detector hits at HEAD must be remediated by one of three forms: citing a ticket ID that resolves in the ticket system, dropping the rot-prone token, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.
The CI guard (check_comment_hygiene.py) runs as a named step in _build-and-test.yml and must reject reintroduced rot-prone refs while passing the current remediated tree with zero suppressions.
Word-triple-alias acceptor pattern must reject path/extension context (e.g., file names with hyphens) to prevent false accepts; sentence-final aliases remain valid.
Census drift from 15 to 16–17 sites during implementation demonstrates active rot accrual and validates the need for CI enforcement.
